message.content: The last common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) was a small, shrew‑like mammal that lived roughly 70 million years ago. It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group that gave rise to many modern placental mammals, including the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong).
